steps.title: Prepare eyedrop solutions
steps.instruction: Make the following solutions using the listed reagents and volumes: (a) DMSO/PNU‑282987/BrdU eye‑drop: dissolve 50 mg PNU‑282987 in 1.66 mL DMSO (100 mM stock, store 4 °C); dissolve 5 mg BrdU in 5 mL DMSO (100 mg mL⁻¹ stock, store –20 °C). Mix 9.8 mL 1× PBS, 100 µL 100 mM PNU‑282987, and 100 µL BrdU stock to obtain 1 mM PNU‑282987 and 1 mg mL⁻¹ BrdU. Store at 4 °C for 1 month. (b) DMSO/BrdU eye‑drop: mix 9.8 mL 1× PBS, 100 µL DMSO, and 100 µL BrdU stock to obtain 1 mg mL⁻¹ BrdU. Store at 4 °C for 1 month.

steps.title: Prepare laboratory buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare the following buffers: (a) 4 % PFA: dissolve 4 g PFA in 100 mL 1× PBS, add 2 M NaOH drops while stirring until pH≈7.4, heat at 85 °C for ~20 min, cool at 4 °C, adjust to pH 6.9 with 1 M HCl, store 4 °C for 1 week. (b) FACS buffer with 4 % FBS: add 4 mL FBS to 96 mL 1× PBS, store 4 °C for 1 month. (c) 0.4 % Triton X‑100: add 4 mL Triton X‑100 to 96 mL 1× PBS, store 4 °C for several months. (d) 0.1 M HCl: add 1.5 mL 1 M HCl to 13.5 mL Milli‑Q water, store at room temperature.

steps.title: Apply eyedrops for 28 days
steps.instruction: Treat adult mice (3–6 month old) daily for 28 days with either (i) 1 % DMSO + 1 mg mL⁻¹ BrdU or (ii) 1 mM PNU‑282987 + 1 mg mL⁻¹ BrdU. Immobilize the mouse by scuffing the neck skin, place one drop of the appropriate solution on the bulbar conjunctiva of the right eye for 1–2 s, then repeat on the left eye.

steps.title: Enucleate and isolate retina
steps.instruction: Euthanize mice by CO₂ asphyxiation. Using Dumont #7 curved forceps, lift each eyeball and place it in a 10 mm Petri dish with 3 mL ice‑cold 1× PBS. Grasp the sclera with Dumont #5 forceps, move the eye out of the dish, make a puncture along the corneal equator with a scalpel, return the eye to the dish, insert spring scissors into the puncture and cut circumferentially. Peel away cornea and iris, remove the lens, evert the posterior eyecup, and cut the retina free with spring scissors. Remove any residual pigmented retinal epithelium. Rinse the isolated retina in a new 10 mm dish containing 3 mL ice‑cold 1× PBS.

steps.title: Digest retina with papain
steps.instruction: Prepare papain solution according to the manufacturer’s instructions and warm 500 µL to 37 °C for ≥10 min. Transfer four retinas into a 1.5 mL tube containing the warm papain, mince into eight pieces with spring scissors, add 25 µL of 1 mg mL⁻¹ DNase I, close the tube and incubate at 37 °C on a rocker for 60 min.

steps.title: Trituration and filtration
steps.instruction: Pour the digestion mixture into a 90 mm Petri dish, rinse the dish with warm EBSS to collect remaining tissue, and triturate with a 10 mL pipette at least five times until the suspension is cloudy and no large pieces remain (avoid bubbles). Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL conical tube and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min.

steps.title: Resuspend cell pellet
steps.instruction: While the tube spins, prepare a resuspension solution containing 2.7 mL EBSS, 300 µL ovomucoid inhibitor, and 150 µL DNase I. After centrifugation, discard the supernatant and add the entire 3.15 mL resuspension solution to the pellet. Triturate 1–2 times with a 10 mL pipette.

steps.title: Density‑gradient separation
steps.instruction: In a new 15 mL tube, add 5 mL ovomucoid inhibitor solution (from step C1). Gently layer the entire cell suspension on top without mixing (tilt the pipette and release on the “slow” setting). Centrifuge at 70 × g for 6 min.

steps.title: Fix cells with PFA
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, resuspend the cell pellet in 2 mL 4 % PFA, and incubate 15 min at room temperature. Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min.

steps.title: Wash with FACS buffer
steps.instruction: Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 2 mL FACS buffer, and centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min.

steps.title: Acid treatment for BrdU detection
steps.instruction: Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 2 mL 0.1 M HCl pre‑warmed to 37 °C, incubate 15 min at 37 °C, then centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min.

steps.title: Permeabilize with Triton
steps.instruction: Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 2 mL 0.4 % Triton X‑100, sit 15 min at room temperature, then centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min.

steps.title: Count cells (optional)
steps.instruction: While the cells are incubating, withdraw 20 µL of suspension and determine cell number using an automated counter or hemocytometer (≈1 × 10⁶ cells per two retinas).

steps.title: Block Fc receptors
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Fc‑block and 50 µL BD Horizon Brilliant Stain Buffer to the cell pellet, mix, and incubate 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash and resuspend for staining
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL FACS buffer, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend cells in 1 mL FACS buffer (triturate 1–2 times with a 1 mL glass pipette). Transfer the suspension to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Prepare compensation beads
steps.instruction: For each fluorophore, place 1 drop compensation beads in a 1.5 mL tube, add 1 µL of the corresponding antibody (see Table 2), vortex, and incubate on ice 30 min. Add 1 mL FACS buffer, centrifuge 150 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 500 µL FACS buffer, and pass through a 70 µm cell strainer into a 5 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Stain for vimentin (Müller glia)
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL streptavidin‑BUV‑395 per 1 × 10⁶ cells to the cell suspension, incubate 30 min at room temperature, then add 500 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 150 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 500 µL FACS buffer, and filter through a 70 µm strainer.

steps.title: Stain for rhodopsin
steps.instruction: In a separate 1.5 mL tube, combine 5 µL mouse α‑Rhodopsin IgG, 5 µL Zenon™ mouse IgG labeling reagent (Component A), and ≤20 µL 1× PBS; incubate 5 min in the dark at room temperature. Add 5 µL Zenon™ blocking reagent (Component B) and incubate another 5 min in the dark. Add the resulting Zenon‑labeled rhodopsin antibody to the cell suspension, incubate 30 min in the dark at room temperature, then add 500 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 150 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend in 500 µL FACS buffer before filtering.

steps.title: Stain with remaining antibodies
steps.instruction: Add the following antibodies to the cell suspension (volumes per 1 × 10⁶ cells, see Table 1): Rhodopsin unconjugated RET‑P1 – 3 µL; Thy1.2‑APC‑eFluor‑780 – 1 µL; Vimentin‑Biotinylated – 2 µL; Ki67‑BUV‑737 – 5 µL; BrdU‑PerCP‑eFluor‑710 – 1 µL. Vortex briefly, incubate 30 min in the dark at room temperature, add 500 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 150 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend in 500 µL FACS buffer. Pass the final stained cells through a 70 µm cell strainer into a 5 mL Falcon tube for acquisition.

description: Validation of protocol Representative results from 28 days of DMSO and PNU-282987 treatment are presented in Figure 4 . Quantitative results are shown in Figure 5 . Figure 4. Representative gating strategy used for gating vimentin+ and Ki67+ cells after 28 days of DMSO and PNU-282987 treatment. (A) and (F) A gate is made around the main cell population to exclude debris (SSC-A vs. FSC-A). (B–C) and (G–H) Singlet gates are drawn using FSC-H vs. FSC-A and SSC-H vs. SSC-A. (D) and (I) Vimentin+ cells are gated using FMOs to determine the cell population positive for vimentin (FSC-A vs. BUV-395-A). Back-gating figure for vimentin, displaying vimentin+ cells in the parent populations, is depicted in Figure S3. (E) and (J) Vimentin+ cells that are also labeled for the proliferation marker Ki67 are gated around. FMOs were utilized to determine positive cell populations (BUV-737-A vs. BUV-395-A). Figure 5. Müller glia and proliferating Müller glia are increased in PNU-282987-treated samples. Adult (3–6 month old) mice were treated with 1× PBS eyedrops containing 1% DMSO and 1 mg/mL BrdU or 1 mM PNU-282987 and 1 mg/mL BrdU for 28 days. Subsequently, retinae were dissociated and processed for analysis by flow cytometry. (A) Graph showing the percent increase of vimentin+ Müller glia cells in DMSO vs. PNU-282987-treated samples. (B) Graph showing the percent increase of vimentin+Ki67+ Müller glia in DMSO vs. PNU-282987-treated samples. Total retinae: DMSO n = 12; PNU-282987 n = 12. Results are based on three independent experiments with retinae from mice pooled in each of the three experiments. Statistics: unpaired t -test with Welch’s correction; *p < 0.05.
